chunks.arabic_text: صَالِحُ بْنُ سَهْلٍ، الْهَمْدَانِيُّ، كُوفِيٌّ. غَالٍ، كَذَّابٌ، وَضَّاعٌ لِلْحَدِيثِ. رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Ṣāliḥ b. Sahl, al-Hamdānī, Kufan. A Ghālī, a liar, a fabricator of ḥadīth. He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him).

chunks.arabic_text: لَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ، وَلَا فِي سَائِرِ مَا رَوَاهُ.

translations.en: There is no good in him, and nor in the rest of what he narrated.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* characterizes Ṣāliḥ b. Sahl al-Hamdānī as a *Ghālī* (exaggerator) whose doctrinal deviations led to his classification as a liar and fabricator. The text’s definitive verdict—that there is 'no good' in him or his narrations—reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking biographical criticism (*al-jarḥ wa al-taʿdīl*) to theological accuracy, ensuring that narrations from the Imams are preserved free from sectarian exaggeration.
en.seo_question: Who is Ṣāliḥ b. Sahl al-Hamdānī and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: A narrator who exaggerates the status of the Imams, often considered a specific category of narrators in Shia scholarship.
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.لَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ: There is no good in him (a phrase indicating weak or unreliable status in hadith transmission).
